implicationsForHeldOutFixes: Real text drew no compound, no -er derivation, no inner Locution and no place-name base, and the sense check flipped 2 real-text attempts, both right. Round 4's held-out-based fixes 1 (sense-led route for a noun-or-verb base), 2 (the sense check as one relative question), 3 (-er's inhabitant sense and place names) and 5 (the inner-Locution floor) would move no real-text attempt; they serve the adversarial classes. Under the lenient tolerance the compound half of fix 1 is moot (Segelboot, Schaukelpferd, Erbrecht, Steuermann pass); its derivation half (Fischer, Kreuzer 🚢) remains.

proposedFixes.fix: A fossilized prefix: drop a prefix analysis whose base's chosen headword is no listed noun (the exact-letters noun test on Fahre)
A suffix base with umlaut and a dropped -e: before -ig and -lich, offer the noun with the umlaut undone and -e restored (Gnade for gnäd)
zu right before a noun inside a phraseme is ADP, by code, as zu closing a slot is PART

verdict: Real text scores 90.0% (81 of 90 attempts; 26 of 30 cases exact on every repetition), strict and lenient alike. The simple words a learner meets most are essentially solved: 62 of 66 attempts on words with no Constituents, every particle verb and three of four derivations. The remaining failures are not rare-word noise: Gefahr, gnädig and Weihnachten are common words and zu Gast sein a common phraseme, and three of the four failures are systematic, code-fixable classes (a fossilized prefix, a base with umlaut and dropped -e, zu before a noun). With 30 cases the interval is wide (4 failing cases).
